title: STEP: Soft Trajectory Estimation of Prediction Correctness via Per-Step Probability Scoring
abstract: arXiv:2610.34537v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Estimating the correctness of large language model (LLM) predictions without access to ground truth is critical for reliable deployment in high-stakes settings. Existing approaches, such as entropy and perplexity, operate solely on final output statistics, discarding the rich information encoded in intermediate reasoning steps. To address this limitation, we propose STEP (Soft Trajectory Estimation of Prediction correctness), a training-free framework that scores each reasoning step via lightweight forward passes to obtain a soft probability distribution qi over candidate answers, from which we derive a set of soft trajectory features capturing per-step confidence and its progression toward the final answer. Extensive experiments on various benchmarks demonstrate consistent and substantial improvements, particularly in AUROC, over output-based baselines and hard-indicator trajectory methods. translated_title: STEP：通过逐步概率评分进行预测正确性的软轨迹估计
translated_abstract: 在无法获取真实标签（ground truth）的情况下估计大型语言模型（LLM）预测的正确性，对于在高风险场景中的可靠部署至关重要。现有方法（如熵和困惑度）仅依赖最终输出的统计信息，丢弃了中间推理步骤中编码的丰富信息。为了解决这一局限性，我们提出了STEP（预测正确性的软轨迹估计），这是一个无需训练的框架，通过轻量级前向传递对每个推理步骤进行评分，从而获得候选答案上的软概率分布qi，并从中推导出一组软轨迹特征，捕捉每一步的置信度及其向最终答案演进的过程。在各种基准测试上的大量实验表明，相较于基于输出的基线方法和硬指标轨迹方法，该方法取得了一致且显著的改进，尤其是在AUROC指标上。值得注意的是，时间加权一致性（Temporally-Weighted Consistency），其……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 提出无需训练的STEP框架，通过对LLM推理的每个中间步骤进行概率评分构建软轨迹特征，在无法获取真实答案的情况下更准确地估计模型预测的正确性。
en_tdlr: STEP is a training-free framework that scores each intermediate reasoning step via lightweight forward passes to build soft trajectory features, enabling more accurate estimation of LLM prediction correctness without access to ground truth.
